Entry Call to Arms The lord used the call order to require vassals, knights and men of suitable age to serve; it seemed to be a paper order, but in fact it tested the prestige, food and trust accumulated by the lord in daily life. The nobles care about who must send troops, while the peasants only care about what will happen to the fields after the family loses labor. Victory or defeat on the battlefield is important, but who can keep the army with horse supplies and silver coins in the second month often determines the length of the war.

The nobles care about who must send troops, while the peasants only care about what will happen to the fields after the family loses labor. They look at whether the flag is at the front, whether the order is clear, and whether the wounded are recovered; a beautiful strategy is not worth singing if it does not allow people to return to the camp alive.

The nobles care about who must send troops, while the peasants only care about what will happen to the fields after the family loses labor. Blacksmiths re-heat broken swords red, priests keep vigil for the dead; the war continues long after it has left the battlefield, on anvils, in graveyards, and on empty seats.

The nobles care about who must send troops, while the peasants only care about what will happen to the fields after the family loses labor. The expedition took away horses, grain, and sons. The flags were changed several times, but they still had to repair houses, bury people, and wait for the next winter; they judged victory or defeat only by whether the village was still there.
